You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.


A shared git remote named 'shared' connects you to teammates working in parallel copies of this repository. Their in-progress branches are fetched for you automatically and announced as [git] notes with changed-file lists. View teammate code: `git diff HEAD...shared/<agent> -- <file>`. Take their version of a file: `git checkout shared/<agent> -- <file>`. Reusing their public names and code avoids conflicts when the work is merged.

## Your Task

## Environment

Toolchains available in this workspace:
gcc: gcc (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0
g++: g++ (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0
make: GNU Make 4.3
cargo: cargo 1.92.0 (344c4567c 2025-10-21)
rustc: rustc 1.92.0 (ded5c06cf 2025-12-08)
go: 
python3: Python 3.10.12

There is NO network access during your run and during grading: any package download (crates.io, proxy.golang.org, pip install) will fail. Write your implementation against the STANDARD LIBRARY of the language you pick, or vendor dependency sources in-tree. Before finishing, verify that `bash compile.sh` produces ./executable.

## Task context

We want to write the source code for a given executable. The executable is
located at `./executable` in the workspace root. You also have access to the
existing documentation (README.md, the man page, and anything else bundled in
the workspace).

## Your task

Implement the source code to generate an executable of exactly identical
behavior as the original.

Rules:
- You MUST create a `./compile.sh` script; running `bash compile.sh` with no
  network access must build your source and produce `./executable` in the
  workspace root. Grading rebuilds from source with your compile.sh — a

## Environment

gcc: gcc (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0
g++: g++ (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0

## Task context

We want to write the source code for a given executable. The executable is
located at `./executable` in the workspace root. You also have access to the

behavior as the original.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# i3-style

Make your i3 config a little more stylish.

About

i3-style applies a theme to your i3 config file to change the colorscheme of window decorations and the different parts of i3bar. It is designed especially for people who frequently change colorschemes.

- Easy to try out new themes.
- Themes are easy to read, modify, and share.
- Modifies your theme in place; templates are not required.

Usage

Call the tool with the name of the theme (or a path to a theme file) and the output location. The tool will apply the theme to your i3 configuration.

Example:

    i3-style solarized -o ~/.config/i3/config --reload

Or apply a theme file directly:

    i3-style ~/.config/i3/solarized.yaml -o ~/.config/i3/config

Send us themes!

If you have a colorscheme you'd like to share, you can convert an existing i3 config to a theme file:

    i3-style --to-theme ~/.config/i3/config -o my-theme.yaml

extra.raw_output:
# i3-style

Make your i3 config a little more stylish.

About

i3-style applies a theme to your i3 config file to change the colorscheme of window decorations and the different parts of i3bar. It is designed especially for people who frequently change colorschemes.

- Easy to try out new themes.
- Themes are easy to read, modify, and share.
- Modifies your theme in place; templates are not required.

Usage

Call the tool with the name of the theme (or a path to a theme file) and the output location. The tool will apply the theme to your i3 configuration.

Example:

    i3-style solarized -o ~/.config/i3/config --reload

Or apply a theme file directly:

    i3-style ~/.config/i3/solarized.yaml -o ~/.config/i3/config

Send us themes!

If you have a colorscheme you'd like to share, you can convert an existing i3 config to a theme file:

    i3-style --to-theme ~/.config/i3/config -o my-theme.yaml

Please consider contributing new themes.

License

This work is available under a FreeBSD-style license (see LICENSE).

All rights reserved.

Make your i3 config a little more stylish.

About

i3-style applies a theme to your i3 config file to change the colorscheme of window decorations and the different parts of i3bar. It is designed especially for people who frequently change colorschemes.

- Easy to try out new themes.
- Themes are easy to read, modify, and share.
- Modifies your theme in place; templates are not required.

Usage

Call the tool with the name of the theme (or a path to a theme file) and the output location. The tool will apply the theme to your i3 configuration.

Example:

    i3-style solarized -o ~/.config/i3/config --reload

Or apply a theme file directly:

# i3-style

Make your i3 config a little more stylish.

About

i3-style applies a theme to your i3 config file to change the colorscheme of window decorations and the different parts of i3bar. It is designed especially for people who frequently change colorschemes.

- Easy to try out new themes.
- Themes are easy to read, modify, and share.
- Modifies your theme in place; templates are not required.

Usage

Call the tool with the name of the theme (or a path to a theme file) and the output location. The tool will apply the theme to your i3 configuration.

Example:

    i3-style solarized -o ~/.config/i3/config --reload

Or apply a theme file directly:

    i3-style ~/.config/i3/solarized.yaml -o ~/.config/i3/config

Send us themes!

If you have a colorscheme you'd like to share, you can convert an existing i3 config to a theme file:

    i3-style --to-theme ~/.config/i3/config -o my-theme.yaml

Please consider contributing new themes.

License

All rights reserved.

+            ("client.focused".to_string(), vec!["#000000".to_string(), "#000000".to_string(), "#ffffff".to_string(), "#000000".to_string()]),
+            ("client.focused_inactive".to_string(), vec!["#000000".to_string(), "#000000".to_string(), "#ffffff".to_string(), "#000000".to_string()]),
+            ("client.unfocused".to_string(), vec!["#000000".to_string(), "#000000".to_string(), "#ffffff".to_string(), "#000000".to_string()]),
+            ("client.urgent".to_string(), vec!["#000000".to_string(), "#000000".to_string(), "#ffffff".to_string(), "#000000".to_string()]),
+        ])),
+        bar_colors: Some(HashMap::from([
+            ("focused_workspace".to_string(), vec!["#000000".to_string(), "#000000".to_string(), "#ffffff".to_string()]),
+            ("active_workspace".to_string(), vec!["#000000".to_string(), "#000000".to_string(), "#ffffff".to_string()]),
+            ("inactive_workspace".to_string(), vec!["#000000".to_string(), "#000000".to_string(), "#ffffff".to_string()]),
+            ("urgent_workspace".to_string(), vec!["#000000".to_string(), "#000000".to_string(), "#ffffff".to_string()]),
+        ])),
+        window_colors: None,
+    }
+}
+
+fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
+    let mut result = HashMap::new();
+    for line in content.lines() {
+        let line = line.trim();
+        if line.starts_with('#') || line.is_empty() {
+            continue;
+        }
+        let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
+        if parts.len() >= 2 {
+            let key = parts[0].to_string();
+            let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
+            result.insert(key, values);
+        }
+    }
+    result
+}
+
+fn format_config(theme: &Theme) -> String {
+    let mut output = String::new();
+    
+    if let Some(colors) = &theme.colors {
+        for (key, values) in colors {
+            output.push_str(&format!("{} {}\n", key, values.join(" ")));
+        }
+    }
+    
+    if let Some(bar_colors) = &theme.bar_colors {
+        for (key, values) in bar_colors {
+            output.push_str(&format!("{} {}\n", key, values.join(" ")));
+        }
+    }
+    
+    if let Some(window_colors) = &theme.window_colors {
+        for (key, values) in window_colors {
+            output.push_str(&format!("{} {}\n", key, values.join(" ")));
+        }
+    }
+    
+    output
+}
+
+fn list_all_themes() {
+    let themes = [
+        "slate", "alphare", "ubuntu", "flat-gray", "purple",
+        "archlinux", "default", "debian", "oceanic-next", "base16-tomorrow",
+        "okraits", "icelines", "solarized", "deep-purple", "tomorrow-night-80s",
+        "seti", "lime", "gruvbox", "mate"
+    ];
+    
+    for theme in themes {
+        println!("{}", theme);
+    }
+}
+
+fn print_help() {
+    println!("Usage: {} [OPTIONS] [THEME]", std::env::args().next().unwrap_or_else(|| "i3-style".to_string()));
+    println!();
+    println!("Options:");
+    println!("  -t, --theme <name>    Apply theme (default: purple)");
+    println!("  -c, --config <path>   Config file path (default: ~/.config/i3/config)");
+    println!("  -l, --list            List all available themes");
+    println!("  -h, --help            Print help information");
+    println!("  -v, --version         Print version information");
+}
+
+fn print_version() {
+    println!("i3-style 1.0.0");
+}
+
+fn main() {
+    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
+    
+    if args.len() > 1 && (args[1] == "-h" || args[1] == "--help") {
+        print_help();
+        return;
+    }
+    
+    if args.len() > 1 && (args[1] == "-v" || args[1] == "--version") {
+        print_version();
+        return;
+    }
+    
+    let mut theme_name: Option<String> = None;
+    let mut config_path: Option<String> = None;
+    let mut list_all = false;
+    
+    let mut i = 2;
+    while i < args.len() {
+        match args[i].as_str() {
+            "-t" | "--theme" => {
+                if i + 1 < args.len() {
+                    theme_name = Some(args[i + 1].clone());
+                    i += 2;
+                } else {
+                    eprintln!("Error: --theme requires a theme name");
+                    process::exit(1);
+                }
+            }
+            "-c" | "--config" => {
+                if i + 1 < args.len() {
+                    config_path = Some(args[i + 1].clone());
+                    i += 2;
+                } else {
+                    eprintln!("Error: --config requires a path");
+                    process::exit(1);
+                }
+            }
+            "-l" | "--list" => {
+                list_all = true;
+                i += 1;
+            }
+            _ => {
+                if theme_name.is_none() {
+                    theme_name = Some(args[i].clone());
+                }
+                i += 1;
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    
+    if list_all {
+        list_all_themes();
+        return;
+    }
+    
+    let theme_name = theme_name.unwrap_or_else(|| "purple".to_string());
+    let config_path = config_path.unwrap_or_else(get_default_config_path);
+    
+    let theme = get_theme_from_name(&theme_name)
+        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
+            eprintln!("Error: Unknown theme '{}'", theme_name);
+            process::exit(1);
+        });
+    
+    if !Path::new(&config_path).exists() {
+        eprintln!("Error: Config file '{}' does not exist", config_path);
+        process::exit(1);
+    }
+    
+    let config_content = fs::read_to_string(&config_path)
+        .unwrap_or_else(|e| {
+            eprintln!("Error: Failed to read config: {}", e);
+            process::exit(1);
+        });
+    
+    let mut config = parse_config(&config_content);
+    
+    if let Some(colors) = &theme.colors {
+        for (key, values) in colors {
+            if let Some(existing_values) = config.get(key) {
+                if existing_values.len() >= 4 {
+                    let new_values: Vec<String> = values.iter().take(4).cloned().collect();
+                    config.insert(key.clone(), new_values);
+                }
+            } else {
+                config.insert(key.clone(), values.clone());
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    
+    if let Some(bar_colors) = &theme.bar_colors {
+        for (key, values) in bar_colors {
+            if let Some(existing_values) = config.get(key) {
+                if existing_values.len() >= 3 {
+                    let new_values: Vec<String> = values.iter().take(3).cloned().collect();
+                    config.insert(key.clone(), new_values);
+                }
+            } else {
+                config.insert(key.clone(), values.clone());
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    
+    if let Some(window_colors) = &theme.window_colors {
+        for (key, values) in window_colors {
+            if let Some(existing_values) = config.get(key) {
+                if existing_values.len() >= 4 {
+                    let new_values: Vec<String> = values.iter().take(4).cloned().collect();
+                    config.insert(key.clone(), new_values);
+                }
+            } else {
+                config.insert(key.clone(), values.clone());
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    
+    let output = format_config(&theme);
+    print!("{}", output);
+}

+fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {

+        if line.starts_with('#') || line.is_empty() {
+            continue;
+        }
+        let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
+        if parts.len() >= 2 {
+            let key = parts[0].to_string();
+            let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
+            result.insert(key, values);
+        }
+    }
+    result

+fn format_config(theme: &Theme) -> String {

+    if let Some(colors) = &theme.colors {

+    if let Some(bar_colors) = &theme.bar_colors {
+        for (key, values) in bar_colors {

# i3-style

Make your i3 config a little more stylish.

About

i3-style applies a theme to your i3 config file to change the colorscheme of window decorations and the different parts of i3bar. It is designed especially for people who frequently change colorschemes.

Usage

Call the tool with the name of the theme (or a path to a theme file) and the output location. The tool will apply the theme to your i3 configuration.

Send us themes!

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::env;
use std::fs;
use std::io::Write;

fn get_default_config_path() -> String {
    let home = env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_else(|_| ".".to_string());
    format!("{}/.i3/config", home)
}

fn get_available_themes() -> Vec<String> {
    vec![
        "slate".to_string(),
        "alphare".to_string(),
        "ubuntu".to_string(),
        "flat-gray".to_string(),
        "purple".to_string(),
        "archlinux".to_string(),
        "default".to_string(),
        "debian".to_string(),
        "oceanic-next".to_string(),
        "base16-tomorrow".to_string(),
        "okraits".to_string(),
        "icelines".to_string(),
        "solarized".to_string(),
        "deep-purple".to_string(),
        "tomorrow-night-80s".to_string(),
        "seti".to_string(),
        "lime".to_string(),
        "gruvbox".to_string(),
        "mate".to_string(),
    ]
}

fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let mut config = HashMap::new();
    for line in content.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.starts_with("statusline") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("statusline".to_string(), values);
            }
        } else if line.starts_with("bar") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("bar".to_string(), values);
            }
        }
    }
    config
}

fn format_config(config: &HashMap<String, Vec<String>>) -> String {

# i3-style

i3-style applies a theme to your i3 config file to change the colorscheme of window decorations and the different parts of i3bar. It is designed especially for people who frequently change colorschemes.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::env;
use std::fs;
use std::io::Write;

fn get_default_config_path() -> String {
    let home = env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_else(|_| ".".to_string());
    format!("{}/.i3/config", home)
}

fn get_available_themes() -> Vec<String> {
    vec![
        "slate".to_string(),
        "alphare".to_string(),
        "ubuntu".to_string(),
        "flat-gray".to_string(),
        "purple".to_string(),
        "archlinux".to_string(),
        "default".to_string(),
        "debian".to_string(),
        "oceanic-next".to_string(),
        "base16-tomorrow".to_string(),
        "okraits".to_string(),
        "icelines".to_string(),
        "solarized".to_string(),
        "deep-purple".to_string(),
        "tomorrow-night-80s".to_string(),
        "seti".to_string(),
        "lime".to_string(),
        "gruvbox".to_string(),
        "mate".to_string(),
    ]
}

fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let mut config = HashMap::new();
    for line in content.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.starts_with("statusline") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("statusline".to_string(), values);
            }
        } else if line.starts_with("bar") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("bar".to_string(), values);
            }
        }
    }
    config
}

fn format_config(config: &HashMap<String, Vec<String>>) -> String {
    let mut output = String::from("# i3 config file (v4)
#
# Please see http://i3wm.org/docs/userguide.html for a complete reference!
#
# This config file uses keycodes (bindsym) and was written for the QWERTY
# layout.
#
# To get a config file with the same key positions, but for your current
# layout, use the i3-config-wizard
#

# Font for window titles. Will also be used by the bar unless a different font
# is used in the bar {} block below. ISO 10646 = Unicode
font -misc-fixed-medium-r-normal--13-120-75-75-C-70-iso10646-1
# The font above is very space-efficient, that is, it looks good, sharp and
# clear in small sizes. However, if you need a lot of unicode glyphs or
# right-to-left text rendering, you should instead use pango for rendering and
# chose a FreeType font, such as:
# font pango:DejaVu Sans Mono 10

# use Mouse+Mod1 to drag floating windows to their wanted position
floating_modifier Mod1

# start a terminal
bindsym Mod1+Return exec i3-sensible-terminal

# kill focused window
bindsym Mod1+Shift+q kill

# start dmenu (a program launcher)
bindsym Mod1+d exec dmenu_run
# There also is the (new) i3-dmenu-desktop which only displays applications
# shipping a .desktop file. So you need that installed.

# change focus

bindsym Mod1+w layout tabbed
bindsym Mod1+e layout toggle split

fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let mut config = HashMap::new();
    for line in content.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.starts_with("statusline") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("statusline".to_string(), values);
            }
        } else if line.starts_with("bar") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("bar".to_string(), values);
            }
        }
    }
    config
}

# shipping a .desktop file. So you need that installed.
# bindsym Mod1+d exec --no-startup-id i3-dmenu-desktop

# change focus
bindsym Mod1+j focus left
bindsym Mod1+k focus down
bindsym Mod1+l focus up
bindsym Mod1+semicolon focus right

# alternatively, you can use the cursor keys:
bindsym Mod1+Left focus left
bindsym Mod1+Down focus down
bindsym Mod1+Up focus up
bindsym Mod1+Right focus right

# move focused window
bindsym Mod1+Shift+j move left
bindsym Mod1+Shift+k move down
bindsym Mod1+Shift+l move up
bindsym Mod1+Shift+semicolon move right

# alternatively, you can use the cursor keys:
bindsym Mod1+Shift+Left move left
bindsym Mod1+Shift+Down move down
bindsym Mod1+Shift+Up move up
bindsym Mod1+Shift+Right move right

# split in horizontal orientation
bindsym Mod1+h split h

# split in vertical orientation
bindsym Mod1+v split v

# enter fullscreen mode for the focused container
bindsym Mod1+f fullscreen

# change container layout (stacked, tabbed, toggle split)
bindsym Mod1+s layout stacking
bindsym Mod1+w layout tabbed
bindsym Mod1+e layout toggle split

# toggle tiling / floating
bindsym Mod1+Shift+space floating toggle

# change focus between tiling / floating windows
bindsym Mod1+space focus mode_toggle

# focus the parent container
bindsym Mod1+a focus parent

# focus the child container
#bindsym Mod1+d focus child

# move the currently focused window to the scratchpad
bindsym Mod1+Shift+minus move scratchpad

# Show the next scratchpad window or hide the focused scratchpad window.
# If there are multiple scratchpad windows, this command cycles through them.
bindsym Mod1+minus scratchpad show

# switch to workspace
bindsym Mod1+1 workspace 1
bindsym Mod1+2 workspace 2
bindsym Mod1+3 workspace 3
bindsym Mod1+4 workspace 4
bindsym Mod1+5 workspace 5
bindsym Mod1+6 workspace 6
bindsym Mod1+7 workspace 7
bindsym Mod1+8 workspace 8
bindsym Mod1+9 workspace 9
bindsym Mod1+0 workspace 10

# move focused window to workspace

use std::collections::HashMap;

fn get_default_config_path() -> String {
    let home = env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_else(|_| ".".to_string());
    format!("{}/.i3/config", home)
}

fn get_available_themes() -> Vec<String> {
    vec![
        "slate".to_string(),
        "alphare".to_string(),
        "ubuntu".to_string(),
        "flat-gray".to_string(),
        "purple".to_string(),
        "archlinux".to_string(),

        "gruvbox".to_string(),
        "mate".to_string(),
    ]
}

fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let mut config = HashMap::new();
    for line in content.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.starts_with("statusline") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("statusline".to_string(), values);
            }
        } else if line.starts_with("bar") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("bar".to_string(), values);
            }
        }
    }
    config
}

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::env;
use std::fs;
use std::io::Write;

fn get_default_config_path() -> String {
    let home = env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_else(|_| ".".to_string());
    format!("{}/.i3/config", home)
}

fn get_available_themes() -> Vec<String> {
    vec![
        "slate".to_string(),
        "alphare".to_string(),
        "ubuntu".to_string(),
        "flat-gray".to_string(),
        "purple".to_string(),
        "archlinux".to_string(),
        "default".to_string(),
        "debian".to_string(),
        "oceanic-next".to_string(),
        "base16-tomorrow".to_string(),
        "okraits".to_string(),
        "icelines".to_string(),
        "solarized".to_string(),
        "deep-purple".to_string(),
        "tomorrow-night-80s".to_string(),
        "seti".to_string(),
        "lime".to_string(),
        "gruvbox".to_string(),
        "mate".to_string(),
    ]
}

fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let mut config = HashMap::new();
    for line in content.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.starts_with("statusline") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("statusline".to_string(), values);
            }
        } else if line.starts_with("bar") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("bar".to_string(), values);
            }
        }
    }
    config
}

fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let mut config = HashMap::new();
    for line in content.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.starts_with("statusline") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("statusline".to_string(), values);
            }
        } else if line.starts_with("bar") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("bar".to_string(), values);
            }
        }
    }
    config
}

fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let mut config = HashMap::new();
    for line in content.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.starts_with("statusline") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("statusline".to_string(), values);
            }
        } else if line.starts_with("bar") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("bar".to_string(), values);
            }
        }
    }
    config
}

fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let mut config = HashMap::new();
    for line in content.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.starts_with("statusline") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("statusline".to_string(), values);
            }
        } else if line.starts_with("bar") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("bar".to_string(), values);
            }
        }
    }
    config
}

fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let mut config = HashMap::new();
    for line in content.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.starts_with("statusline") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("statusline".to_string(), values);
            }
        } else if line.starts_with("bar") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("bar".to_string(), values);
            }
        }
    }
    config
}

# Please see http://i3wm.org/docs/userguide.html for a complete reference!
#
# This config file uses keycodes (bindsym) and was written for the QWERTY
# layout.
#
# To get a config file with the same key positions, but for your current
# layout, use the i3-config-wizard
#

# Font for window titles. Will also be used by the bar unless a different font
# is used in the bar {} block below. ISO 10646 = Unicode
font -misc-fixed-medium-r-normal--13-120-75-75-C-70-iso10646-1
# The font above is very space-efficient, that is, it looks good, sharp and
# clear in small sizes. However, if you need a lot of unicode glyphs or
# right-to-left text rendering, you should instead use pango for rendering and
# chose a FreeType font, such as:
# font pango:DejaVu Sans Mono 10

# use Mouse+Mod1 to drag floating windows to their wanted position
floating_modifier Mod1

# start a terminal
bindsym Mod1+Return exec i3-sensible-terminal

# kill focused window
bindsym Mod1+Shift+q kill

# start dmenu (a program launcher)
bindsym Mod1+d exec dmenu_run
# There also is the (new) i3-dmenu-desktop which only displays applications
# shipping a .desktop file. It is a wrapper around dmenu, so you need that
# installed.
# bindsym Mod1+d exec --no-startup-id i3-dmenu-desktop

# change focus
bindsym Mod1+j focus left
bindsym Mod1+k focus down
bindsym Mod1+l focus up
bindsym Mod1+semicolon focus right

# alternatively, you can use the cursor keys:
bindsym Mod1+Left focus left
bindsym Mod1+Down focus down
bindsym Mod1+Up focus up
bindsym Mod1+Right focus right

# move focused window
bindsym Mod1+Shift+j move left
bindsym Mod1+Shift+k move down
bindsym Mod1+Shift+l move up
bindsym Mod1+Shift+semicolon move right

# alternatively, you can use the cursor keys:
bindsym Mod1+Shift+Left move left
bindsym Mod1+Shift+Down move down
bindsym Mod1+Shift+Up move up
bindsym Mod1+Shift+Right move right

# split in horizontal orientation
bindsym Mod1+h split h

# split in vertical orientation
bindsym Mod1+v split v

# enter fullscreen mode for the focused container
bindsym Mod1+f fullscreen

# change container layout (stacked, tabbed, toggle split)
bindsym Mod1+s layout stacking
bindsym Mod1+w layout tabbed
bindsym Mod1+e layout toggle split

# toggle tiling / floating
bindsym Mod1+Shift+space floating toggle

# change focus between tiling / floating windows
bindsym Mod1+space focus mode_toggle

# focus the parent container
bindsym Mod1+a focus parent

# focus the child container
#bindsym Mod1+d focus child

bindsym Mod1+Shift+minus move scratchpad

# Show the next scratchpad window or hide the focused scratchpad window.

fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let mut config = HashMap::new();
    for line in content.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.starts_with("statusline") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("statusline".to_string(), values);
            }
        } else if line.starts_with("bar") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("bar".to_string(), values);
            }
        }
    }
    config
}

fn parse_config(content: &str) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let mut config = HashMap::new();
    for line in content.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.starts_with("statusline") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {
                let values: Vec<String> = parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                config.insert("statusline".to_string(), values);
            }
        } else if line.starts_with("bar") {
            let parts: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
            if parts.len() >= 2 {

def parse_config_file(config_path):
    """Parse an i3 config file and extract relevant information."""
    if not os.path.exists(config_path):
        return None
    
    with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
        content = f.read()
    
    # Extract font
    font_match = re.search(r'^font\s+(.+)$', content, re.MULTILINE)
    font = font_match.group(1).strip() if font_match else None
    
    # Extract bars section
    bar_match = re.search(r'bar\s*\{([^}]*(?:\{[^}]*\}[^}]*)*)\}', content, re.DOTALL)
    bar_colors = {}
    if bar_match:
        bar_content = bar_match.group(1)
        colors_match = re.search(r'colors\s*\{([^}]*)\}', bar_content, re.DOTALL)
        if colors_match:
            colors_content = colors_match.group(1)
            for color_name in ['separator', 'background', 'statusline']:
                color_match = re.search(rf'{color_name}\s+([^#\n]+)', colors_content)
                if color_match:
                    bar_colors[color_name] = color_match.group(1).strip()
    
    # Extract client colors
    client_colors = {}
    for client_type in ['focused', 'focused_inactive', 'unfocused', 'urgent']:
        client_match = re.search(rf'client\.{client_type}\s+([^#\n]+)', content)
        if client_match:
            client_colors[client_type] = client_match.group(1).strip()
    
    return {
        'font': font,
        'bar_colors': bar_colors,
        'client_colors': client_colors,
    }


def apply_theme_to_config(config_path, theme_name, output_path=None, save_to_input=False):
    """Apply a theme to an i3 config file."""
    config_data = parse_config_file(config_path)
    
    if config_data is None:
        print("Could not find i3 config")
        return False
    
    theme = get_theme(theme_name)
    if theme is None:
        print(f"Theme '{theme_name}' not found")
        return False
    
    # Generate output
    output_lines = []
    
    # Font line
    if config_data['font']:
        output_lines.append(config_data['font'])
    
    # Bar section
    if config_data['bar_colors']:
        output_lines.append("")
        output_lines.append("bar {")
        output_lines.append("  colors {")
        for color_name, color_value in config_data['bar_colors'].items():
            output_lines.append(f"    {color_name} #{color_value}")
        output_lines.append("  }")
        output_lines.append("}")
    
    # Client colors
    if config_data['client_colors']:
        output_lines.append("")
        for client_type, colors in config_data['client_colors'].items():
            output_lines.append(f"client.{client_type} #{colors[0]} #{colors[1]} #{colors[2]} #{colors[3]}")
    
    # Write output
    if output_path:
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write('\n'.join(output_lines) + '\n')
    
    if save_to_input:
        # Save input to temp location
        temp_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'i3-style')
        os.makedirs(temp_dir, exist_ok=True)
        temp_input = os.path.join(temp_dir, f"{int(time.time())}/config-input")
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(temp_input), exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(config_path, temp_input)
        print(f"saving config at {config_path} to {temp_input}")
    
    return True


def get_theme(theme_name):
    """Get theme definition by name."""
    if theme_name in BUILTIN_THEMES:
        return BUILTIN_THEMES[theme_name]
    return None


def list_themes():
    """List all available themes."""
    print("\nAvailable themes:")
    for name, description in sorted(BUILTIN_THEMES.items()):
        print(f"  {name:20} - {description}")


def to_theme(config_path):
    """Convert a config file to a theme YAML file."""
    config_data = parse_config_file(config_path)
    
    if config_data is None:
        print("Could not find i3 config")
        return False
    
    # Extract colors from config
    colors = {}
    if config_data['bar_colors']:
        for color_name, color_value in config_data['bar_colors'].items():
            colors[color_name] = f"#{color_value}"
    
    # Extract client colors
    window_colors = {}
    for client_type in ['focused', 'focused_inactive', 'unfocused', 'urgent']:
        if client_type in config_data['client_colors']:
            colors_list = config_data['client_colors'][client_type].split()
            if len(colors_list) >= 4:
                window_colors[client_type] = {
                    'border': colors_list[0],
                    'background': colors_list[1],
                    'text': colors_list[2],
                    'indicator': colors_list[3],
                }
    
    # Generate YAML output
    output_lines = ["---"]
    output_lines.append("meta:")
    output_lines.append("  description: AUTOMATICALLY GENERATED THEME")
    output_lines.append("colors:")
    for color_name, color_value in sorted(colors.items()):
        output_lines.append(f'  {color_name}: "{color_value}"')
    output_lines.append("window_colors:")
    for client_type in ['focused', 'focused_inactive', 'unfocused', 'urgent']:
        if client_type in window_colors:
            output_lines.append(f"  {client_type}:")
            for key, value in window_colors[client_type].items():
                output_lines.append(f"    {key}: {value}")
    output_lines.append("bar_colors:")
    output_lines.append(f"  background: {colors.get('background', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"  statusline: {colors.get('statusline', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"  separator: {colors.get('separator', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append("  focused_workspace:")
    output_lines.append(f"    border: {colors.get('focused_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"    background: {colors.get('focused_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"    text: {colors.get('focused_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append("  urgent_workspace:")
    output_lines.append(f"    border: {colors.get('urgent_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"    background: {colors.get('urgent_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"    text: {colors.get('urgent_workspace', '#000000')}")
    
    print('\n'.join(output_lines))
    return True


def validate_config(config_path):
    """Validate an i3 config file using i3."""
    import subprocess
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ['i3', '-C', '-c', config_path],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=10
        )
        if result.returncode != 0:
            print(f"Could not validate config with `i3 -C -c {config_path}` (is i3 in the PATH?) {result.stderr.strip()}")
            return False
        return True
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"Could not validate config with `i3 -C -c {config_path}` (is i3 in the PATH?) No such file or directory (os error 2)")
        return False
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Could not validate config with `i3 -C -c {config_path}` (is i3 in the PATH?) {str(e)}")
        return False


def reload_config(config_path):
    """Reload i3 config."""
    import subprocess
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ['i3-msg', 'reload'],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=10
        )
        if result.returncode != 0:
            print(f"Could not reload config with i3-msg: {result.stderr.strip()}")
            return False
        return True
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"Could not reload config with i3-msg: No such file or directory (os error 2)")
        return False
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Could not reload config with i3-msg: {str(e)}")
        return False


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description='Make your i3 config a bit more stylish',
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
        epilog='''
Examples:
  i3-style solarized -o ~/.config/i3/config --reload
  i3-style ~/.config/i3/solarized.yaml -o ~/.config/i3/config
  i3-style --to-theme ~/.config/i3/config -o my-theme.yaml
        '''
    )
    
    parser.add_argument('-h', '--help', action='store_true', help='Prints help information')
    parser.add_argument('-l', '--list-all', action='store_true', help='Print a list of all available themes')
    parser.add_argument('-r', '--reload', action='store_true', help='Apply the theme by reloading the config')
    parser.add_argument('-s', '--save', action='store_true', help='Set the output file to the path of the input file')
    parser.add_argument('-V', '--version', action='store_true', help='Prints version information')
    parser.add_argument('-c', '--config', metavar='<file>', help='The config file the theme should be applied to. Defaults to the default i3 location.')
    parser.add_argument('-o', '--output', metavar='<file>', help='Apply the theme, attempt to validate the result, and write it to <file>')
    parser.add_argument('-t', '--to-theme', metavar='<file>', help='Prints an i3-style theme based on the given config suitable for sharing with others')
    parser.add_argument('theme', nargs='?', help='The theme to use')
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    if args.help:
        parser.print_help()
        return 0
    
    if args.version:
        print(f"i3-style {VERSION}")
        return 0
    
    if args.list_all:
        list_themes()
        return 0
    
    if args.to_theme:
        if not args.config:
            print("Error: --to-theme requires a config file")
            return 1
        return to_theme(args.config)
    
    if not args.theme:
        print("Error: theme argument is required")
        return 1
    
    # Determine config path
    config_path = args.config if args.config else DEFAULT_CONFIG
    
    # Apply theme
    if not apply_theme_to_config(config_path, args.theme, args.output, args.save):
        return 1
    
    # Validate if output specified
    if args.output:
        if not validate_config(args.output):
            return 1
    
    # Reload if requested
    if args.reload:
        if not reload_config(config_path):
            return 1
    
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

def parse_config_file(config_path):
    """Parse an i3 config file and extract relevant information."""
    if not os.path.exists(config_path):
        return None
    
    with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
        content = f.read()
    
    # Extract font
    font_match = re.search(r'^font\s+(.+)$', content, re.MULTILINE)
    font = font_match.group(1).strip() if font_match else None
    
    # Extract bars section
    bar_match = re.search(r'bar\s*\{([^}]*(?:\{[^}]*\}[^}]*)*)\}', content, re.DOTALL)
    bar_colors = {}
    if bar_match:
        bar_content = bar_match.group(1)
        colors_match = re.search(r'colors\s*\{([^}]*)\}', bar_content, re.DOTALL)
        if colors_match:
            colors_content = colors_match.group(1)
            for color_name in ['separator', 'background', 'statusline']:
                color_match = re.search(rf'{color_name}\s+([^#\n]+)', colors_content)
                if color_match:
                    bar_colors[color_name] = color_match.group(1).strip()
    
    # Extract client colors
    client_colors = {}
    for client_type in ['focused', 'focused_inactive', 'unfocused', 'urgent']:
        client_match = re.search(rf'client\.{client_type}\s+([^#\n]+)', content)
        if client_match:
            client_colors[client_type] = client_match.group(1).strip()
    
    return {
        'font': font,
        'bar_colors': bar_colors,
        'client_colors': client_colors,
    }


def apply_theme_to_config(config_path, theme_name, output_path=None, save_to_input=False):
    """Apply a theme to an i3 config file."""
    config_data = parse_config_file(config_path)
    
    if config_data is None:
        print("Could not find i3 config")
        return False
    
    theme = get_theme(theme_name)
    if theme is None:
        print(f"Theme '{theme_name}' not found")
        return False
    
    # Generate output
    output_lines = []
    
    # Font line
    if config_data['font']:
        output_lines.append(config_data['font'])
    
    # Bar section
    if config_data['bar_colors']:
        output_lines.append("")
        output_lines.append("bar {")
        output_lines.append("  colors {")
        for color_name, color_value in config_data['bar_colors'].items():
            output_lines.append(f"    {color_name} #{color_value}")
        output_lines.append("  }")
        output_lines.append("}")
    
    # Client colors
    if config_data['client_colors']:
        output_lines.append("")
        for client_type, colors in config_data['client_colors'].items():
            output_lines.append(f"client.{client_type} #{colors[0]} #{colors[1]} #{colors[2]} #{colors[3]}")
    
    # Write output
    if output_path:
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write('\n'.join(output_lines) + '\n')
    
    if save_to_input:
        # Save input to temp location
        temp_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'i3-style')
        os.makedirs(temp_dir, exist_ok=True)
        temp_input = os.path.join(temp_dir, f"{int(time.time())}/config-input")
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(temp_input), exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(config_path, temp_input)
        print(f"saving config at {config_path} to {temp_input}")
    
    return True


def get_theme(theme_name):
    """Get theme definition by name."""
    if theme_name in BUILTIN_THEMES:
        return BUILTIN_THEMES[theme_name]
    return None

def to_theme(config_path):
    """Convert a config file to a theme YAML file."""
    config_data = parse_config_file(config_path)
    
    if config_data is None:
        print("Could not find i3 config")
        return False
    
    # Extract colors from config
    colors = {}
    if config_data['bar_colors']:
        for color_name, color_value in config_data['bar_colors'].items():
            colors[color_name] = f"#{color_value}"
    
    # Extract client colors
    window_colors = {}
    for client_type in ['focused', 'focused_inactive', 'unfocused', 'urgent']:
        if client_type in config_data['client_colors']:
            colors_list = config_data['client_colors'][client_type].split()
            if len(colors_list) >= 4:
                window_colors[client_type] = {
                    'border': colors_list[0],
                    'background': colors_list[1],
                    'text': colors_list[2],
                    'indicator': colors_list[3],
                }
    
    # Generate YAML output
    output_lines = ["---"]
    output_lines.append("meta:")
    output_lines.append("  description: AUTOMATICALLY GENERATED THEME")
    output_lines.append("colors:")
    for color_name, color_value in sorted(colors.items()):
        output_lines.append(f'  {color_name}: "{color_value}"')
    output_lines.append("window_colors:")
    for client_type in ['focused', 'focused_inactive', 'unfocused', 'urgent']:
        if client_type in window_colors:
            output_lines.append(f"  {client_type}:")
            for key, value in window_colors[client_type].items():
                output_lines.append(f"    {key}: {value}")
    output_lines.append("bar_colors:")
    output_lines.append(f"  background: {colors.get('background', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"  statusline: {colors.get('statusline', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"  separator: {colors.get('separator', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append("  focused_workspace:")
    output_lines.append(f"    border: {colors.get('focused_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"    background: {colors.get('focused_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"    text: {colors.get('focused_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append("  urgent_workspace:")
    output_lines.append(f"    border: {colors.get('urgent_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"    background: {colors.get('urgent_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"    text: {colors.get('urgent_workspace', '#000000')}")
    
    print('\n'.join(output_lines))
    return True


def validate_config(config_path):
    """Validate an i3 config file using i3."""
    import subprocess
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ['i3', '-C', '-c', config_path],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=10
        )
        if result.returncode != 0:
            print(f"Could not validate config with `i3 -C -c {config_path}` (is i3 in the PATH?) {result.stderr.strip()}")
            return False
        return True
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"Could not validate config with `i3 -C -c {config_path}` (is i3 in the PATH?) No such file or directory (os error 2)")
        return False
    except Exception as e:

def parse_config_file(config_path):
    """Parse an i3 config file and extract relevant information."""
    if not os.path.exists(config_path):
        return None
    
    with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
        content = f.read()
    
    # Extract font
    font_match = re.search(r'^font\s+(.+)$', content, re.MULTILINE)
    font = font_match.group(1).strip() if font_match else None
    
    # Extract bars section
    bar_match = re.search(r'bar\s*\{([^}]*(?:\{[^}]*\}[^}]*)*)\}', content, re.DOTALL)
    bar_colors = {}
    if bar_match:
        bar_content = bar_match.group(1)
        colors_match = re.search(r'colors\s*\{([^}]*)\}', bar_content, re.DOTALL)
        if colors_match:
            colors_content = colors_match.group(1)
            for color_name in ['separator', 'background', 'statusline']:
                color_match = re.search(rf'{color_name}\s+([^#\n]+)', colors_content)
                if color_match:
                    bar_colors[color_name] = color_match.group(1).strip()
    
    # Extract client colors
    client_colors = {}
    for client_type in ['focused', 'focused_inactive', 'unfocused', 'urgent']:
        client_match = re.search(rf'client\.{client_type}\s+([^#\n]+)', content)
        if client_match:
            client_colors[client_type] = client_match.group(1).strip()
    
    return {
        'font': font,
        'bar_colors': bar_colors,
        'client_colors': client_colors,
    }


def apply_theme_to_config(config_path, theme_name, output_path=None, save_to_input=False):
    """Apply a theme to an i3 config file."""
    config_data = parse_config_file(config_path)
    
    if config_data is None:
        print("Could not find i3 config")
        return False
    
    theme = get_theme(theme_name)
    if theme is None:
        print(f"Theme '{theme_name}' not found")
        return False
    
    # Generate output
    output_lines = []
    
    # Font line
    if config_data['font']:
        output_lines.append(config_data['font'])
    
    # Bar section
    if config_data['bar_colors']:
        output_lines.append("")
        output_lines.append("bar {")
        output_lines.append("  colors {")
        for color_name, color_value in config_data['bar_colors'].items():
            output_lines.append(f"    {color_name} #{color_value}")
        output_lines.append("  }")
        output_lines.append("}")
    
    # Client colors
    if config_data['client_colors']:
        output_lines.append("")
        for client_type, colors in config_data['client_colors'].items():
            output_lines.append(f"client.{client_type} #{colors[0]} #{colors[1]} #{colors[2]} #{colors[3]}")
    
    # Write output
    if output_path:
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write('\n'.join(output_lines) + '\n')
    
    if save_to_input:
        # Save input to temp location
        temp_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'i3-style')
        os.makedirs(temp_dir, exist_ok=True)
        temp_input = os.path.join(temp_dir, f"{int(time.time())}/config-input")
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(temp_input), exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(config_path, temp_input)
        print(f"saving config at {config_path} to {temp_input}")
    
    return True


def get_theme(theme_name):
    """Get theme definition by name."""
    if theme_name in BUILTIN_THEMES:
        return BUILTIN_THEMES[theme_name]
    return None


def list_themes():
    """List all available themes."""
    print("\nAvailable themes:")
    for name, description in sorted(BUILTIN_THEMES.items()):
        print(f"  {name:20} - {description}")


def to_theme(config_path):
    """Convert a config file to a theme YAML file."""
    config_data = parse_config_file(config_path)
    
    if config_data is None:
        print("Could not find i3 config")
        return False
    
    # Extract colors from config
    colors = {}
    if config_data['bar_colors']:
        for color_name, color_value in config_data['bar_colors'].items():
            colors[color_name] = f"#{color_value}"
    
    # Extract client colors
    window_colors = {}
    for client_type in ['focused', 'focused_inactive', 'unfocused', 'urgent']:
        if client_type in config_data['client_colors']:
            colors_list = config_data['client_colors'][client_type].split()
            if len(colors_list) >= 4:
                window_colors[client_type] = {
                    'border': colors_list[0],
                    'background': colors_list[1],
                    'text': colors_list[2],
                    'indicator': colors_list[3],
                }
    
    # Generate YAML output
    output_lines = ["---"]
    output_lines.append("meta:")
    output_lines.append("  description: AUTOMATICALLY GENERATED THEME")
    output_lines.append("colors:")
    for color_name, color_value in sorted(colors.items()):
        output_lines.append(f'  {color_name}: "{color_value}"')
    output_lines.append("window_colors:")
    for client_type in ['focused', 'focused_inactive', 'unfocused', 'urgent']:
        if client_type in window_colors:
            output_lines.append(f"  {client_type}:")
            for key, value in window_colors[client_type].items():
                output_lines.append(f"    {key}: {value}")
    output_lines.append("bar_colors:")
    output_lines.append(f"  background: {colors.get('background', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"  statusline: {colors.get('statusline', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"  separator: {colors.get('separator', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append("  focused_workspace:")
    output_lines.append(f"    border: {colors.get('focused_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"    background: {colors.get('focused_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"    text: {colors.get('focused_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append("  urgent_workspace:")
    output_lines.append(f"    border: {colors.get('urgent_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"    background: {colors.get('urgent_workspace', '#000000')}")
    output_lines.append(f"    text: {colors.get('urgent_workspace', '#000000')}")
    
    print('\n'.join(output_lines))
    return True


def validate_config(config_path):
    """Validate an i3 config file using i3."""
    import subprocess
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ['i3', '-C', '-c', config_path],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=10
        )
        if result.returncode != 0:
            print(f"Could not validate config with `i3 -C -c {config_path}` (is i3 in the PATH?) {result.stderr.strip()}")
            return False
        return True
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"Could not validate config with `i3 -C -c {config_path}` (is i3 in the PATH?) No such file or directory (os error 2)")
        return False
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Could not validate config with `i3 -C -c {config_path}` (is i3 in the PATH?) {str(e)}")
        return False


def reload_config(config_path):
    """Reload i3 config."""
    import subprocess
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ['i3-msg', 'reload'],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=10
        )
        if result.returncode != 0:
            print(f"Could not reload config with i3-msg: {result.stderr.strip()}")
            return False
        return True
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"Could not reload config with i3-msg: No such file or directory (os error 2)")
        return False
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Could not reload config with i3-msg: {str(e)}")
        return False


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description='Make your i3 config a bit more stylish',
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
        epilog='''
Examples:
  i3-style solarized -o ~/.config/i3/config --reload
  i3-style ~/.config/i3/solarized.yaml -o ~/.config/i3/config
  i3-style --to-theme ~/.config/i3/config -o my-theme.yaml
        '''
    )
    
    parser.add_argument('-h', '--help', action='store_true', help='Prints help information')
    parser.add_argument('-l', '--list-all', action='store_true', help='Print a list of all available themes')
    parser.add_argument('-r', '--reload', action='store_true', help='Apply the theme by reloading the config')
    parser.add_argument('-s', '--save', action='store_true', help='Set the output file to the path of the input file')
    parser.add_argument('-V', '--version', action='store_true', help='Prints version information')
    parser.add_argument('-c', '--config', metavar='<file>', help='The config file the theme should be applied to. Defaults to the default i3 location.')
    parser.add_argument('-o', '--output', metavar='<file>', help='Apply the theme, attempt to validate the result, and write it to <file>')
    parser.add_argument('-t', '--to-theme', metavar='<file>', help='Prints an i3-style theme based on the given config suitable for sharing with others')
    parser.add_argument('theme', nargs='?', help='The theme to use')
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    if args.help:
        parser.print_help()
        return 0
    
    if args.version:
        print(f"i3-style {VERSION}")
        return 0
    
    if args.list_all:
        list_themes()
        return 0
    
    if args.to_theme:
        if not args.config:
            print("Error: --to-theme requires a config file")
            return 1
        return to_theme(args.config)
    
    if not args.theme:
        print("Error: theme argument is required")
        return 1
    
    # Determine config path
    config_path = args.config if args.config else DEFAULT_CONFIG
    
    # Apply theme
    if not apply_theme_to_config(config_path, args.theme, args.output, args.save):
        return 1
    
    # Validate if output specified
    if args.output:
        if not validate_config(args.output):
            return 1
    
    # Reload if requested
    if args.reload:
        if not reload_config(config_path):
            return 1
    
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

            return True
        except Exception as e:

def main():
    """Main entry point"""

    if verbose:
        print(f"Applying theme '{theme_name}' to {config_path}")
    
    # Read the config file
    try:
        with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
            config_content = f.read()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error reading config file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    # Get theme colors and window states
    colors = get_theme_colors(theme_name)
    states = get_window_states(theme_name)
    
    if not colors:
        print(f"Error: Unknown theme '{theme_name}'", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    if verbose:
        print(f"Theme colors: {list(colors.keys())}")
    
    # Apply theme to config
    modified = False
    
    # Replace color variables
    for color_name, color_value in colors.items():
        # Match color_name: #hex
        pattern = rf'\b{color_name}:\s*#[0-9a-fA-F]{{6}}\b'
        matches = re.findall(pattern, config_content)
        if matches:
            if verbose:
                print(f"Found {len(matches)} occurrences of {color_name}")
            config_content = re.sub(pattern, f'{color_name}: {color_value}', config_content)
            modified = True

    for state_name, state_colors in states.items():
        for prop, value in state_colors.items():
            # Match state_name { border: #hex, ... }
            pattern = rf'\b{state_name}\s*\{{[^}}]*\}}'
            matches = re.findall(pattern, config_content)

                    print(f"Found {len(matches)} occurrences of {state_name}")
                config_content = re.sub(pattern, f'{state_name} {state_colors}', config_content)

    else:

    if theme_name in WINDOW_STATES:

    return None

def apply_theme_to_config(config_path, theme_name, output_path=None, dry_run=False, verbose=False):
    """Apply a theme to an i3 config file"""
    if not os.path.exists(config_path):
        print(f"Error: Config file not found: {config_path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    if verbose:
        print(f"Applying theme '{theme_name}' to {config_path}")
    
    # Read the config file
    try:
        with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
            config_content = f.read()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error reading config file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    # Get theme colors and window states
    colors = get_theme_colors(theme_name)
    states = get_window_states(theme_name)
    
    if not colors:
        print(f"Error: Unknown theme '{theme_name}'", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    if verbose:
        print(f"Theme colors: {list(colors.keys())}")
    
    # Apply theme to config
    modified = False
    
    # Replace color variables
    for color_name, color_value in colors.items():
        # Match color_name: #hex
        pattern = rf'\b{color_name}:\s*#[0-9a-fA-F]{{6}}\b'
        matches = re.findall(pattern, config_content)
        if matches:
            if verbose:
                print(f"Found {len(matches)} occurrences of {color_name}")
            config_content = re.sub(pattern, f'{color_name}: {color_value}', config_content)
            modified = True
    
    # Apply window states
    for state_name, state_colors in states.items():
        for prop, value in state_colors.items():
            # Match state_name { border: #hex, ... }
            pattern = rf'\b{state_name}\s*\{{[^}}]*\}}'
            matches = re.findall(pattern, config_content)
            if matches:
                if verbose:
                    print(f"Found {len(matches)} occurrences of {state_name}")
                config_content = re.sub(pattern, f'{state_name} {state_colors}', config_content)
                modified = True
    
    if not modified:
        print("No changes made to config file", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    if dry_run:
        print("Dry run - no changes made")
        print("\n--- Modified config would look like ---")
        print(config_content)
        print("--- End of modified config ---\n")
        return True
    
    # Write to output file or overwrite
    if output_path:
        try:
            with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(config_content)
            if verbose:
                print(f"Theme applied to {output_path}")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error writing output file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return False
    else:
        try:
            with open(config_path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(config_content)
            if verbose:
                print(f"Theme applied to {config_path}")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error writing config file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return False

def main():
    """Main entry point"""
    args = parse_args()
    
    # If no theme specified, show help

        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
            prog="i3-style",

            epilog="Use --help for more information."

def parse_args():
    """Parse command line arguments"""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="i3-style",
        description="Apply themes to i3 config files",
        epilog="Use --help for more information."
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "theme",
        nargs="?",
        choices=list(BUILTIN_THEMES.keys()),
        help="Theme to apply (see --help for list)"
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "-c", "--config",
        default=DEFAULT_CONFIG,
        help=f"Path to i3 config file (default: {DEFAULT_CONFIG})"
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "-o", "--output",
        help="Output file (default: overwrite config file)"
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "-d", "--dry-run",
        action="store_true",
        help="Show what would be changed without making changes"
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "-v", "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        help="Print verbose output"
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "--version",
        action="version",
        version=f"%(prog)s {VERSION}"
    )
    
    return parser.parse_args()

def get_theme_colors(theme_name):
    """Get colors for a theme"""
    if theme_name in THEME_DEFINITIONS:
        return THEME_DEFINITIONS[theme_name]
    return None

def get_window_states(theme_name):
    """Get window states for a theme"""
    if theme_name in WINDOW_STATES:
        return WINDOW_STATES[theme_name]
    return None

def apply_theme_to_config(config_path, theme_name, output_path=None, dry_run=False, verbose=False):
    """Apply a theme to an i3 config file"""
    if not os.path.exists(config_path):
        print(f"Error: Config file not found: {config_path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    if verbose:
        print(f"Applying theme '{theme_name}' to {config_path}")
    
    # Read the config file
    try:
        with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
            config_content = f.read()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error reading config file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    # Get theme colors and window states
    colors = get_theme_colors(theme_name)
    states = get_window_states(theme_name)
    
    if not colors:
        print(f"Error: Unknown theme '{theme_name}'", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    if verbose:
        print(f"Theme colors: {list(colors.keys())}")
    
    # Apply theme to config
    modified = False
    
    # Replace color variables
    for color_name, color_value in colors.items():
        # Match color_name: #hex
        pattern = rf'\b{color_name}:\s*#[0-9a-fA-F]{{6}}\b'
        matches = re.findall(pattern, config_content)
        if matches:
            if verbose:
                print(f"Found {len(matches)} occurrences of {color_name}")
            config_content = re.sub(pattern, f'{color_name}: {color_value}', config_content)
            modified = True
    
    # Apply window states
    for state_name, state_colors in states.items():
        for prop, value in state_colors.items():
            # Match state_name { border: #hex, ... }
            pattern = rf'\b{state_name}\s*\{{[^}}]*\}}'
            matches = re.findall(pattern, config_content)
            if matches:
                if verbose:
                    print(f"Found {len(matches)} occurrences of {state_name}")
                config_content = re.sub(pattern, f'{state_name} {state_colors}', config_content)
                modified = True
    
    if not modified:
        print("No changes made to config file", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    if dry_run:
        print("Dry run - no changes made")
        print("\n--- Modified config would look like ---")
        print(config_content)
        print("--- End of modified config ---\n")
        return True
    
    # Write to output file or overwrite
    if output_path:
        try:
            with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(config_content)
            if verbose:
                print(f"Theme applied to {output_path}")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error writing output file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return False
    else:
        try:
            with open(config_path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(config_content)
            if verbose:
                print(f"Theme applied to {config_path}")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error writing config file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return False

def main():
    """Main entry point"""
    args = parse_args()
    
    # If no theme specified, show help
    if args.theme is None:
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
            prog="i3-style",
            description="Apply themes to i3 config files",
            epilog="Use --help for more information."
        )
        parser.print_help()
        return 0
    
    # Apply theme
    success = apply_theme_to_config(
        args.config,
        args.theme,
        args.output,
        args.dry_run,
        args.verbose
    )
    
    return 0 if success else 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
EOF"}

About

bindsym Mod1+Shift+9 move container to workspace 9
bindsym Mod1+Shift+0 move container to workspace 10

# exit i3 (logs you out of your X session)

        # Pressing down will grow the window’s height.
        bindsym j           resize shrink width 10 px or 10 ppt

        bindsym semicolon   resize grow width 10 px or 10 ppt

        bindsym Left        resize shrink width 10 px or 10 ppt
        bindsym Down        resize grow height 10 px or 10 ppt
        bindsym Up          resize shrink height 10 px or 10 ppt

def parse_args():
    """Parse command line arguments"""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="i3-style",
        description="Apply themes to i3 config files",
        epilog="Use --help for more information."
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "theme",
        nargs="?",
        choices=list(BUILTIN_THEMES.keys()),
        help="Theme to apply (see --help for list)"
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "-c", "--config",
        default=DEFAULT_CONFIG,
        help=f"Path to i3 config file (default: {DEFAULT_CONFIG})"
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "-o", "--output",
        help="Output file (default: overwrite config file)"
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "-d", "--dry-run",
        action="store_true",
        help="Show what would be changed without making changes"
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "-v", "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        help="Print verbose output"
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "--version",
        action="version",
        version=f"%(prog)s {VERSION}"
    )
    
    return parser.parse_args()
```

def apply_theme_to_config(config_path, theme_name, output_path=None, dry_run=False, verbose=False):
    """Apply a theme to an i3 config file"""
    if not os.path.exists(config_path):
        print(f"Error: Config file not found: {config_path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    if verbose:
        print(f"Applying theme '{theme_name}' to {config_path}")
    
    # Read the config file
    try:
        with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
            config_content = f.read()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error reading config file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    # Get theme colors and window states
    colors = get_theme_colors(theme_name)
    states = get_window_states(theme_name)
    
    if not colors:
        print(f"Error: Unknown theme '{theme_name}'", file=sys.stderr)

        print(f"Theme colors: {list(colors.keys())}")

    modified = False

def apply_theme_to_config(config_path, theme_name, output_path=None, dry_run=False, verbose=False):
    """Apply a theme to an i3 config file"""
    if not os.path.exists(config_path):
        print(f"Error: Config file not found: {config_path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    if verbose:
        print(f"Applying theme '{theme_name}' to {config_path}")
    
    # Read the config file
    try:
        with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
            config_content = f.read()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error reading config file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    # Get theme colors and window states
    colors = get_theme_colors(theme_name)
    states = get_window_states(theme_name)
    
    if not colors:
        print(f"Error: Unknown theme '{theme_name}'", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    if verbose:
        print(f"Theme colors: {list(colors.keys())}")
    
    # Apply theme to config
    modified = False
    
    # Replace color variables
    for color_name, color_value in colors.items():
        # Match color_name: #hex
        pattern = rf'\b{color_name}\s*#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}\b'
        matches = re.findall(pattern, config_content)
        if matches:
            if verbose:
                print(f"Found {len(matches)} occurrences of {color_name}")
            config_content = re.sub(pattern, f'{color_name}: {color_value}', config_content)
            modified = True
    
    # Apply window states
    for state_name, state_colors in states.items():
        for prop, value in state_colors.items():
            # Match state_name { border: #hex, ... }
            pattern = rf'\b{state_name}\s*\{{[^}}]*\}}'
            matches = re.findall(pattern, config_content)
            if matches:
                if verbose:
                    print(f"Found {len(matches)} occurrences of {state_name}")
                config_content = re.sub(pattern, f'{state_name} {state_colors}', config_content)
                modified = True
    
    if not modified:
        print("No changes made to config file", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    
    if dry_run:
        print("Dry run - no changes made")
        print("\n--- Modified config would look like ---")
        print(config_content)
        print("--- End of modified config ---\n")
        return True
    
    # Write to output file or overwrite
    if output_path:
        try:
            with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(config_content)
            if verbose:
                print(f"Theme applied to {output_path}")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error writing output file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return False
    else:
        try:
            with open(config_path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(config_content)
            if verbose:
                print(f"Theme applied to {config_path}")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error writing config file: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return False

You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Their in-progress branches are fetched for you automatically and announced as [git] notes with changed-file lists. View teammate code: `git diff HEAD...shared/<agent> -- <file>`. Take their version of a file: `git checkout shared/<agent> -- <file>`. Reusing their public names and code avoids conflicts when the work is merged.

## Your Task

## Environment

Toolchains available in this workspace:
gcc: gcc (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0
g++: g++ (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0
make: GNU Make 4.3
cargo: cargo 1.92.0 (344c4567c 2025-10-21)
rustc: rustc 1.92.0 (ded5c06cf 2025-12-08)
go: 
python3: Python 3.10.12

There is NO network access during your run and during grading: any package download (crates.io, proxy.golang.org, pip install) will fail. Write your implementation against the STANDARD LIBRARY of the language you pick, or vendor dependency sources in-tree. Before finishing, verify that `bash compile.sh` produces ./executable.

## Task context

We want to write the source code for a given executable. The executable is
located at `./executable` in the workspace root. You also have access to the
existing documentation (README.md, the man page, and anything else bundled in
the workspace).

## Your task

Implement the source code to generate an executable of exactly identical
behavior as the original.

Rules:
- You MUST create a `./compile.sh` script; running `bash compile.sh` with no
  network access must build your source and produce `./executable` in the
  workspace root. Grading rebuilds from source with your compile.sh — a
  submission without a working compile.sh scores zero.
- Do NOT wrap, shim, or delegate to the provided `./executable`.
- Do NOT decompile the provided `./executable` or use strace/ltrace on it.
- You MAY run the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe
  its behavior, and read all documentation files.
- Behavior to match includes: --help and --version output, flag handling and
  error messages, exit codes, and the program's visible behavior.

Work in the workspace root. Verify your build (`bash compile.sh`) and compare
your program's behavior against the original before finishing.

TEAMMATES: agent1 (feature None), agent2 (feature None) are implementing their features RIGHT NOW in parallel copies of this repo; your diffs will be merged at the end. Coordinate via the send_message tool (incoming messages appear as [Message from ...]): agree on shared names/signatures early and avoid editing the same regions.

## Recommended Workflow

This workflow should be done step-by-step so that you can iterate on your changes and any possible problems.

1. Analyze the codebase by finding and reading relevant files
2. Create a script to reproduce the issue
3. Edit the source code to resolve the issue
4. Verify your fix works by running your script again
5. Test edge cases to ensure your fix is robust
6. Submit your changes — see the **Submission** section below for the exact procedure.

## Command Execution Rules

You are operating in an environment where

1. You issue at least one command
2. The system executes the command(s) in a subshell
3. You see the result(s)
4. You write your next command(s)

Each response should include:

1. **Reasoning text** where you explain your analysis and plan
2. At least one tool call with your command

**CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:**

- Your response SHOULD include reasoning text explaining what you're doing
